lessons.title: Computer Basics: Input, Processing and Output
lessons.notes_html:
What is a Computer?

A computer is an electronic data processing machine. It accepts data (input), processes it, and gives information (output).

Example: We type 2 + 4 on the keyboard (input). The computer processes it and shows 6 on the screen (output).

Hardware and Software

HardwareSoftware
The physical parts of the computer that we can touch, e.g. keyboard, mouse and display unit.Programs — a set of instructions that tell the computer what to do, e.g. MS Windows, Linux and Paint.

Input and Output Devices

Input DevicesOutput Devices
Send data to the computer for processing, e.g. keyboard, mouse and scanner.Deliver the processed information to the user, e.g. monitor, printer and speaker.

mcqs.q: What is a computer?
options: A machine that only prints pictures
A box used only for playing games
mcqs.why: The book defines a computer as an electronic data processing machine. It accepts data (input), processes it, and gives information (output).

mcqs.q: In the book's example, 2 + 4 is typed on the keyboard and the computer shows:
mcqs.why: 2 + 4 is the input, the computer processes it, and the output shown is 6. This small example shows input, processing and output.

mcqs.q: The data we give to a computer is called:
mcqs.why: Data given to the computer is input. After processing, the result the computer gives back is output (information).

mcqs.q: The information a computer gives after processing is called:
mcqs.why: The processed result is called output. Input is the data we give, hardware is the physical parts, and a program is a set of instructions.

mcqs.q: Which of these is hardware?
mcqs.why: The keyboard is a physical part we can touch, so it is hardware. Windows, Paint and Linux are programs, so they are software.

mcqs.q: Software is:
options: A set of instructions (programs) that tell the computer what to do
The parts of the computer we can touch
The power cable of the computer
mcqs.why: Software consists of programs — sets of instructions — that tell the computer what to do, such as MS Windows, Linux and Paint.

mcqs.q: Which device sends data INTO the computer?
mcqs.why: A scanner sends data into the computer, so it is an input device. The monitor, printer and speaker give information out, so they are output devices.

mcqs.q: Which device shows the processed information to the user?
mcqs.why: The monitor is an output device that shows text, pictures and video information to the user. The keyboard, mouse and scanner are input devices.

mcqs.q: Which pair contains only input devices?
mcqs.why: The keyboard and mouse both send data into the computer. The monitor, printer and speaker are all output devices.

mcqs.q: MS Windows and Linux are examples of:
mcqs.why: Windows and Linux are programs that tell the computer what to do, so they are software, not physical parts or devices.

lessons.title: Storage and Processing Devices
lessons.notes_html:
Storage Devices

Storage devices keep data and information safe so we can use them later. Five storage devices are:

  • Hard Disk Drive
  • CD
  • DVD
  • Blu-ray Disc
  • USB flash drive

How Much Data Can They Store?

DeviceStorage Capacity
CD700 MB
DVD4.7 GB
Blu-ray Disc25 GB

A memory card is also used to store data and information. A USB flash drive is small and portable, so files can easily be carried from one place to another.

Processing Devices

Processing devices process data, turn it into information, and help store it in memory. They include the microprocessor (CPU), ROM, RAM and the motherboard.

lessons.title: Generations of Computers
lessons.notes_html:

GenerationYearsKey Features
First1940–1950Vacuum tubes; very large and expensive; produced much heat and used much electricity

lessons.title: Uses of ICT
lessons.notes_html:
ICT in Education

  • Educational games help students learn new concepts.
  • Through online learning (such as Khan Academy and Virtual University) students can study different subjects.
  • The interactive whiteboard helps the teacher teach with videos and pictures.
  • Computers are also used for research, simulation and collaborative work.

ICT in Industry

  • Robots help make and assemble things in factories.
  • Computer-controlled machines make work accurate and fast.
  • Computers manage the record and supply of goods in the warehouse.

Benefits of ICT for Students

  • Wide access to educational resources
  • Learning through interactive games and video-sharing apps
  • Learning from platforms such as Khan Academy and Duolingo
  • Communication through email and social media
  • Cooperation in joint projects
  • Creative work with tools such as Paint and Canva

Disadvantages of ICT for Beginners

  • Distraction — wrong use or lack of supervision affects students' performance.
  • Health problems — eye strain, lack of sleep and physical health problems.
  • Cyber security risks — virus, malware, hacking and phishing attacks.
  • Dependence — overuse of devices makes a person dependent on them.

lessons.title: Devices and Their Functions — Part 1
lessons.notes_html:
Router

A router connects two or more networks together. For example, a home router connects the home network to the internet service provider (ISP). Routers are used for exchanging data between networks.

Network Switch

A network switch is a communication device. It is used to connect computers together in a network.

LAN Card

A LAN card (Network Interface Card) connects the computer to a Local Area Network, through which the computer connects to other computers and communication devices.

QR Code Scanner

A QR code scanner reads the data of a barcode or QR code and sends it to the computer for processing.

Touch Pad

On a touch pad, the cursor on the screen is moved simply by the movement of a finger or stylus (pen). A drawing pad helps in drawing, and a game pad helps in playing games.

Headphone

A headphone is an audio output device that works like a speaker — it delivers the sound of the computer's information directly to the listener's ears.

mcqs.why: A network switch is a communication device — it is used to connect computers together in a network.

lessons.title: Devices and Their Functions — Part 2
lessons.notes_html:
Projector

A projector connects the computer to a screen and shows text, graphics and video information on a large screen.

Microprocessor

The microprocessor is the processing brain of the computer — it processes data. It equals thousands of integrated circuits on a single chip, gives fast performance, is small in size, and produces little heat.

Motherboard

The motherboard is the main board of the computer, on which all the hardware parts of the computer are connected, such as the power supply, microprocessor, RAM, ROM and storage devices.

Flash Drive

A USB flash drive is used to store digital information. It is small and portable, so files can easily be transferred from one place to another.

Remember: Output Devices

Output devices are the devices used for getting information from the computer — for example the monitor, printer and speaker.

lessons.title: Identify the Devices
lessons.notes_html:
Devices Shown in the Book's Pictures

  • Bluetooth adapter — a small USB device labelled Bluetooth with a small cable attached. It is a communication device that enables the computer to exchange data wirelessly with nearby devices.
  • Network Interface Card (LAN card) — a card with an antenna attached, which fits inside the computer. It connects the computer to a network.
  • Plotter — a large printing device printing a map or drawing on large paper. It prints maps and large pictures on large paper, plastic or flex.
  • Motherboard — a green circuit board with many parts and slots fitted on it. It is the main board of the computer.
  • Monitor — a square screen standing on a stand. It is the basic output device, which shows the computer's text, picture and video information.
  • Printer — a device printing a coloured picture on paper. It prints text and graphics information on paper.
  • Scanner — a device fitted above an open book, capturing the image of the book's pages. It converts the picture of paper or a book into digital data and sends it to the computer.
  • Game pad (game controller) — a hand-held controller with buttons and joysticks on it. It is an input device used for playing games.
  • Router — a black box with three antennas fitted on it. It connects two or more networks together.

One Special Device

An interactive (smart) board can be used both for sending data in and for getting the result out, because we can write and touch on it, and it also shows information.

lessons.title: Types of Devices
lessons.notes_html:
The Five Types of Devices

TypeWorkExamples from the Book
Input devicesSend data into the computerTrack ball mouse, barcode scanner
Output devicesGive information out to the userPrinter
Storage devicesStore data and programsMemory card, hard disk drive, SSD
Processing devicesProcess data and hold it during processingROM, microprocessor, RAM
Communication devicesConnect computers togetherNetwork switch
  • ROM chips hold the instructions for starting the computer.
  • RAM is temporary memory, in which running programs and data stay during processing.
  • The hard disk drive and SSD store data and programs permanently.

Two Types of Software

  • System software — the type of software used to manage and control the computer, e.g. Windows, macOS and Linux.
  • Application software — the type of software used to help the user in everyday tasks, e.g. word processing, MS Paint, games and Chrome.

Group Activities in the Book

  • Draw some parts of the computer hardware on a drawing sheet: keyboard (typing data), mouse (moving the cursor), monitor (showing information), system unit (processing) and printer (printing on paper).
  • Prepare a poster presentation on any ICT topic, e.g. "ICT in education", with a title, 3–4 short points, matching pictures and a short conclusion.

mcqs.why: A memory card is used to store data and information, so it is a storage device.

mcqs.why: Moving the ball of the track ball mouse moves the cursor, so it is an input device — a device for sending data in.

lessons.title: Operating System and the Taskbar
lessons.notes_html:
Operating System

An operating system is a program that controls and manages all the parts and programs of the computer, so that using the computer becomes simple and easy for a person. Its main functions are:

  • Managing resources
  • Providing an environment to the user
  • Running programs
  • Managing files
  • Security

The Taskbar in Windows 10

The taskbar is a horizontal strip at the bottom of the desktop. It organises the different Windows features and gives quick access to them, such as: opening applications, searching, viewing the date and time, changing settings, and so on.

Search Box

The "Type here to search" box is used to search for files, folders, applications, settings and things on the web; as soon as a word is typed in it, the matching results appear.

System Tray (Notification Area)

This is the right-hand part of the taskbar, which shows system states such as the battery level, sound, network connection, date and time, and gives access to their settings.

Notepad

Notepad is a simple writing program present in Windows, which is included in every edition of Windows.

lessons.notes_html:
File Explorer

File Explorer in Windows 10 is used for viewing and organising files and folders.

Folder

A folder is a box or container for organising and storing files; different kinds of files can be kept in separate folders. Its icon is a yellow folder.

Recycle Bin

The Recycle Bin is a special folder in Windows in which deleted files and folders stay safely stored for some time, so that they can be brought back if needed. Its icon shows a basket-like picture.

Making a Shortcut

In Windows 10, by right-clicking on a selected file or folder, one can make its shortcut by choosing Create Shortcut from the menu that appears.

Making an Outline and Filling Colour

  • Then choose the "Fill with color" tool from the Tools box.
  • Pick the required colour from the colour palette and click inside the shape, so the inside gets filled with colour.
  • To change the outline or the inside colour, select the Colour 1 or Colour 2 box and choose a new colour.

Colour Palette

The Colour palette holds many colours to choose from for filling colour in a drawing.

Undo Shortcut

In MS Paint, the CTRL+Z keyboard shortcut is pressed to take back (undo) the last action performed.

lessons.title: Steps of Problem Solving
lessons.notes_html:
The Six Problem-Solving Stages

  • 1. Identify the problem — know exactly what the problem is.
  • 2. Gather information — collect facts about it.
  • 3. Review possible solutions — think of the different ways.
  • 4. Choose the best solution — pick the best way.
  • 5. Carry out the solution — act on the chosen way.
  • 6. Evaluate the result — check whether the solution worked.

Example: A Birthday Gift for a Friend

  • 1. Identify — which gift to give the friend.
  • 2. Gather information — think about the friend's likes, the budget and the shops.
  • 3. Review solutions — a book, a game, a gift voucher or a photo album.
  • 4. Choose the best — a special photo album of the friend's memories.
  • 5. Carry out — collect photos and make the album.
  • 6. Evaluate — if the friend is happy the solution worked, otherwise change the plan.

Example: Ali Has a Severe Headache

  • Identify — Ali has a severe headache and needs treatment.
  • Gather information — how long the pain has lasted, whether there is fever or other symptoms.
  • Review solutions — rest, water, medicine or going to the doctor.
  • Choose the best — consult the doctor.
  • Act — go to the doctor and follow the advice.
  • Evaluate — if the pain eases the solution worked, otherwise contact the doctor again.

Benefits of the Step-by-Step Way

The step-by-step way is clear and organised; no step is forgotten, each step can be tested separately, a mistake shows up quickly, the work can be repeated, and everyone can easily understand the instructions. It also reduces the risk of failure: every step is fixed in advance, the order does not get mixed up, and if the result is not good you can go back to step 2 and change the plan.

lessons.title: Breaking a Problem into Parts
lessons.notes_html:
What is Breaking a Problem Down?

Breaking a problem down means dividing it into small parts. Dividing a problem helps us understand each part of the problem better.

Example: Building a Lego Castle

  • Split the castle into parts — base, walls, towers, doors and roof.
  • Separate the pieces and colours needed for each part.
  • Build one part at a time.
  • Finally join all the parts to complete the castle.

Dividing makes the big task easy and understandable.

Why Divide a Big Problem?

A big problem looks difficult all at once. Small parts are easier to understand, solve and test; the facts, input, output and instructions of each part become clear, and then all the parts together give the full solution.

Example: Buying Household Items

  • 1. Make a list of which items are needed.
  • 2. Check the money and budget.
  • 3. Decide the route to the shop.
  • 4. Choose the items in the shop and compare prices.
  • 5. Pay and buy the items.
  • 6. Bring the items home and put them away.

lessons.title: Loops, Pseudocode and Flowcharts
lessons.notes_html:
Algorithm: Multiplication Table of a Number

  • 1. Start
  • 2. Enter the number N
  • 3. Set Count = 1
  • 4. Print N × Count
  • 5. Set Count = Count + 1
  • 6. While Count is not more than 10, go back to step 4
  • 7. Stop

Repeating steps like this is called a loop.

Algorithm: Has the Student Passed?

  • 1. Start
  • 2. Enter the marks of four subjects
  • 3. Find Total = sum of the four marks
  • 4. Find Percentage = Total ÷ 400 × 100 (each subject is out of 100)
  • 5. If the percentage is more than 60, print Pass, otherwise print Fail
  • 6. Stop

Algorithm: Add the First Five Numbers

  • 1. Start
  • 2. Set Sum = 0 and Count = 1
  • 3. Set Sum = Sum + Count
  • 4. Set Count = Count + 1
  • 5. While Count is not more than 5, go back to step 3
  • 6. Print Sum (answer 15)
  • 7. Stop

Pseudocode and Flowcharts

Pseudocode is an easy way of writing an algorithm using everyday language. In a flowchart, the shapes and arrows guide us during the working-through (process) of the instructions or plan.

Algorithmic Thinking

Algorithmic thinking means solving a problem step by step in an organised way — like a detective who finds the solution to a secret.

mcqs.why: The algorithm sets Count = 1, prints N × Count, increases Count by 1, and repeats while Count is not more than 10.

mcqs.why: The loop goes back while Count is not more than 10, so the table is printed up to 10.

mcqs.q: After printing N × Count, Count becomes:
mcqs.why: Step 5 sets Count = Count + 1, so the next line of the table is printed in the next round of the loop.

mcqs.q: The table loop continues while Count is:
mcqs.why: Step 6 says: while Count is not more than 10, go back to step 4. When Count passes 10, the algorithm stops.

mcqs.why: The algorithm takes the marks of four subjects as input and finds the percentage of the marks obtained.

mcqs.q: In the pass/fail algorithm, the percentage is found by:
mcqs.why: Each subject is out of 100, so four subjects make 400. Percentage = Total ÷ 400 × 100.

mcqs.q: If a student's percentage is more than 60, the algorithm shows the student as:
mcqs.why: The rule in the algorithm: if the marks obtained are more than 60 percent, show the student as passed, otherwise failed.

mcqs.q: The sum of the first five numbers (1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5) is:
mcqs.why: The loop adds 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 one by one: Sum becomes 1, 3, 6, 10 and finally 15, which the algorithm prints.

lessons.title: Control Blocks: Repeat, Wait and Decisions
lessons.notes_html:
The Control Block

The control block manages the flow of the script. With it, the program can be paused, a task repeated, and conditional decision instructions given.

Repeat

The block used for repetition in Scratch is Repeat — it repeats the instructions inside it as many times as the given number.

Wait

Wait is the construct used for waiting a short time — it pauses the program for the given number of seconds.

If Block

We check whether a particular condition is true with the If block — if the condition is true, the instructions inside it run.

If-Else

If-else is the construct used for making a decision — if the condition is true one set of instructions runs, and if it is false the other set runs.

Move Block

We use the Move block to move the sprite forward by the given number of steps.

When is a Conditional Statement Used?

A conditional statement is used when what happens next depends on whether a condition is true or false. If the condition is true, one action happens; if it is false, another action happens or nothing happens — as in the body-temperature example or the key-press example.

Code: Move 10 Steps, Repeat 10 Times

To move the sprite only 10 steps and repeat that action 10 times, we need:

  • The green-flag event block,
  • inside it the control block that repeats 10 times,
  • and inside that the motion block that moves 10 steps.

With this, the sprite moves 100 steps in total.

Making a Round Design

Under the space-key-pressed event block, put four motion blocks that turn 90 degrees each, so the sprite completes a full circle (4 × 90 = 360 degrees). For back-and-forth movement, add the move block and the bounce-on-edge block, and put a wait block between turns so the movement is clearly visible.

Debugging: Fixing Bugs

The teacher should guide students through the six-step debugging cycle:

  • 1. Plan the program
  • 2. Write the code
  • 3. Run the program
  • 4. Find the errors
  • 5. Find the cause of the errors
  • 6. Correct the errors and test the program again

Example Bug: The Invisible Turns

The sprite turns 90 degrees four times on the space key, but the turning is not visible. The bug is that all four turns happen at once with no pause. Fix: put a control Wait 1 seconds block after each turn, then run the program again and check that each turn is seen separately.

How Many Times Will the Loop Blocks Run?

  • The repeat-10 block runs ten times.
  • The repeat-until block keeps running until the given condition is met, such as pressing the space key.
  • The forever block never stops and keeps repeating the instructions inside it.

Digital citizenship teaches us to use the internet and ICT in a safe, responsible and ethical way.

Importance of Digital Citizenship

Digital citizenship teaches us to use the internet and ICT in a safe, responsible and ethical way. It helps us protect our personal information and other people's rights, avoid harmful material and illegal acts, and be good citizens in the online world.

Digital Literacy

Digital literacy means the skill of evaluating, accessing and using online material. A good digital citizen has the knowledge needed to use information properly.

How to Behave Towards People Online

Online you should always be kind, polite and respectful. You should not use abusive language or hurtful comments for anyone, bully anyone, or look down on anyone's post with rudeness.

Ethical Issues Linked to ICT Use

  • 1. Misuse of personal information — a name, photo, birth date or home address can fall into wrong hands.

lessons.title: Health Problems from ICT Use
lessons.notes_html:
Six Health Problems Linked to ICT Devices

  • 1. Eye strain — staring at a screen too long tires the eyes, so follow the 20-20-20 rule.
  • 2. Poor body posture — sitting wrongly causes pain and physical harm.
  • 3. Inactive lifestyle and obesity — sitting too long makes the body inactive and increases weight.
  • 4. Disturbed sleep — using devices before bedtime disturbs sleep.
  • 5. Effects of radiating rays — using devices for too long can cause harm, so screen time should be limited.
  • 6. Mental health problems — overuse can cause disappointment, helplessness and depression. Spending too much time on screens can leave us feeling tired and depressed.

Sitting Correctly

  • The top of the computer monitor should be at eye level or slightly below it.
  • The screen should be 18 to 25 inches away from the eyes.
  • Your hands should be kept parallel to the floor.

Group Activity

Each group prepares a presentation on one health problem caused by overuse of ICT — such as eye strain, poor posture, obesity, disturbed sleep, effects of rays, or mental health — and suggests ways to reduce its risk, such as the 20-20-20 rule, sitting correctly, limiting screen time, play and exercise, and switching devices off before bed.

lessons.title: What is Business?
lessons.notes_html:
Business and Businessperson

A businessperson is someone who opens and runs their own business to earn a profit or bear a loss. Every trade started to earn profit is called a business.

Innovation

A new idea or innovation means thinking of new and better ideas. An innovative businessperson always brings forward new ideas and concepts. People who want to start a business should work on new and different ideas — finding a new idea and working on it is the first step in starting a business.

Facing Failure

When faced with failure, a successful businessperson tries again and learns from mistakes. A successful businessperson treats failure as a lesson and tries again with hard work.

Businesspeople and the Country

Businesspeople create new markets and expand existing markets, increasing the country's growth. The business process is a continuous (never-ending) process, which helps the business grow.

Technology in Business

Technology helps businesspeople use tools and gadgets to run their business better, such as digital marketing, mobile apps, artificial intelligence and collaboration tools.

What is a Business Plan?

A business plan is written guidance for starting a business — a detailed written plan made before starting a business. It covers:

  • Operations
  • Funds needed

Identifying an Opportunity — The First Stage

Identifying an opportunity is the first stage of the business process. In it, the businessperson looks for a new business opportunity or idea, and gathers information about it and analyses it. The finding an opportunity stage needs the ability to research and analyse, and creative thinking, to create something new. It needs a creative mind.

The Greatest Quality of a Successful Businessperson

The greatest quality is hard work and never giving up. A hard-working person overcomes failures and disappointments, seizes opportunities, learns from mistakes and tries again. A good idea alone, without hard work, cannot make any business succeed.

How Do Businesspeople Sell Their Goods or Services?

Traditional way: They sell face-to-face through a shop or stall, or through distributors, and publicise their goods with posters, newspaper, radio and TV adverts.

Digital way: They sell through websites, online shops, social media, email marketing, search engine optimisation and online adverts.

lessons.title: Business Activities with Digital Marketing
lessons.notes_html:
Activity: Setting Up a Food Stall

Each class group sets up a food stall (such as samosas, chaat or salad) in the school ground with a budget of 1000 rupees, writing all expenses in a table.

  • Make an expense table (ingredients, utensils, etc.).
  • Add up all expenses to get the total cost.
  • Subtract total cost from total sales income.
  • If income is higher, there is a profit; if lower, there is a loss.

This activity gives students real experience of running a business.

Digital Marketing for the Stall

Design a poster for the stall (stall name, items, prices and an attractive picture), then post it on the school's Facebook page or WhatsApp group. This develops students' creative skills and shows them that advertising plays a key role in promoting a business.

Telling the World About Your City's Famous Product

Each student chooses their city's famous product — for example, Hyderabad's bangles or Nawabshah's Sindhi parat — and uses creativity and social media platforms such as Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp to introduce that product to the world, and helps local people sell it.

Success Stories: Two Groups

  • One group presents the success story of a famous traditional Pakistani businessperson, such as Hakim Muhammad Saeed (Hamdard).
  • The other group presents a famous digital Pakistani businessperson, such as Salim Ghauri (NetSol) or Monis Rahman (Rozee).
